overview: Make chunks searchable via hybrid lexical + semantic retrieval (tsvector + pgvector IVFFlat) and expose a deterministic IDs-only hybridSearch() contract for downstream features like chat.
goals: Upgrade chunking from per-page chunks to small deterministic chunks suitable for citations.
Enable lexical retrieval via tsvector + GIN for chunks.
Enable semantic retrieval via pgvector embeddings + IVFFlat with conservative, data-aware index creation.
Provide a single hybridSearch() function that returns ranked chunk IDs + metadata (IDs-only contract).
Provide a dev-only debug spike endpoint to make retrieval tuning and failures visible.
nonGoals: OCR/layout geometry and precise highlight polygons.
A full retrieval eval harness beyond minimal tests/debug endpoint.
successMetrics: For a seeded pack folder, a representative query retrieves relevant chunk(s) in the top K results (manual proof acceptable for v0).
Chunks are materially smaller than whole pages and carry deterministic metadata for citations.
Debug endpoint outputs tuning context (lists/probes/hit counts) so retrieval can be tuned without guesswork.

stack.hosting: Local dev (docker-compose) today; target deployments vary but must support Postgres + pgvector.
stack.auth: PoC: no end-user auth; dev-only spike endpoints are gated (SPIKES_ENABLED) and some admin-only endpoints require X-Orbital-Admin-Token.

routes.name: Hybrid Search Debug (Spike)
routes.purpose: Dev-only endpoint to run hybridSearch() for a folder/index_version/query and inspect hits + tuning knobs.

inScope: Upgrade chunking from per-page to small deterministic chunks (char window) suitable for citations.
Add lexical index for chunks (tsvector + GIN).
Add semantic index for chunks (pgvector embeddings + IVFFlat) with conservative, data-aware creation.
Implement hybridSearch() as an IDs-only retrieval contract for downstream features (chat hydrates separately).
Implement retrieval as two DB queries (lexical + semantic) and merge/dedupe in TypeScript for debuggability.
Optional: extract the pure merge/scoring logic into packages/core; keep DB + embeddings + logging in apps/web.
Add a dev-only debug endpoint under /spikes/* (apps/web) to validate retrieval.

importFormat.description: Hybrid retrieval inputs are query-time parameters (folderId + indexVersion + queryText) that produce ranked chunk hits (IDs-only).

chunking.determinism: Deterministic for (document_id, index_version); re-ingest produces identical chunk boundaries and hashes.

functionalRequirements: FR-001: Chunking must be deterministic for a given (document_id, index_version) input.
FR-002: Hybrid retrieval must be IDs-only at the contract boundary (return chunk IDs + metadata).
FR-003: Lexical retrieval uses Postgres tsvector query strategy suitable for user input (websearch_to_tsquery).
FR-004: Semantic retrieval uses pgvector cosine distance and supports IVFFlat.
FR-005: Vector index creation must be explicit and safe for small datasets (threshold + conservative lists).
FR-006: Debug-only routes must live under /spikes/* and be gated (no new dev-only endpoints at target paths).
failureStatesUx: If pgvector extension is missing/unavailable: degrade to lexical-only (semantic branch disabled) and make it observable in logs and the debug endpoint.
If embeddings provider fails: ingest fails closed for that document/index_version and surfaces a safe error state.
Never return raw provider payloads or stack traces to clients; use the standard error envelope.

logs: {nVectors, lists, probes, kLex, kSem, kFinal, hitCountsLex, hitCountsSem} for debug endpoint calls.

rollbackDisablePlan: Feature flag the semantic branch (vector search) so the system can run lexical-only if needed.
Ability to drop/recreate IVFFlat index when vector counts grow and tuning changes.

ivfflatIndexingStrategy.notes: Avoid creating IVFFlat with unrealistic lists on tiny datasets; log lists/probes/nVectors for tuning.

rules: Chunking must be deterministic for a given (document_id, index_version) input.
hybridSearch() must return an IDs-only contract (chunk IDs + metadata), not hydrated chunk text.
apps/web owns the hybridSearch() server-only orchestrator (DB + embeddings + logs). packages/core may own pure merge/scoring helpers (no DB/provider/framework dependencies).

If pgvector is missing/unavailable, semantic retrieval is disabled and hybridSearch() degrades to lexical-only; this must be explicit/observable (logs + debug endpoint) and must not silently pretend semantic search is working.
Vector indexing must avoid IVFFlat tiny-dataset footguns by creating the index conservatively and logging tuning context (lists/probes/nVectors).
Debug-only routes must live under /spikes/* and be gated; do not add new dev-only endpoints at target paths.
verificationPlan: Unit test: same input text => same chunk boundaries and hashes.
Integration: ingest a 2-page fixture PDF and observe chunks count > page count.
Schema validation: columns exist and indexes exist.
Integration: stub vectors in DB and validate semantic query ordering.
Unit test: merge scoring is deterministic.
Manual: run debug endpoint against a fixture pack folder and inspect top hits.
Automated: small golden-questions smoke fixture (3-10 queries) asserts an expected doc/page appears in top K for a seeded fixture folder.

dependencies: AI Gateway embedding model wrapper (assumed in PRD0).

stories.title: Deterministic small chunking on ingest
stories.description: As a developer, I want ingest to produce small deterministic chunks per page so that citations and retrieval operate on meaningful units.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-001: Ingest replaces 1 chunk per page with deterministic char-window chunking (max_chars=1500, overlap_chars=200) and boundaries prefer whitespace when possible.
AC-002: Chunk metadata persists in chunks.metadata_json including chunker_id='char_window_v0', page_number, char_start, char_end.
AC-003: Chunk uniqueness remains idempotent via UNIQUE(document_id, index_version, chunk_index).
Example: Ingest a 2-page fixture PDF and observe chunks count > page count for a given index_version.
Negative: If ingest hits an external cap (e.g. MAX_PAGES or other ingest limit), ingest fails closed for that document/index_version and does not write partial chunk rows.

stories.title: Lexical + vector fields exist on chunks and are indexed safely
stories.description: As a developer, I want chunks to support both lexical and semantic retrieval so that exact-term and conceptual queries can find evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-004: chunks gains columns: text_tsv tsvector; embedding vector(1536); embedding_model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'openai/text-embedding-3-small'; embedded_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL.

AC-006: Semantic indexing exists: pgvector extension enabled (otherwise semantic retrieval disabled and system degrades to lexical-only, explicitly observable); IVFFlat index on embedding vector_cosine_ops is created conservatively.
Example: Stub vectors in DB and validate semantic query ordering by embedding <=> query_vector (cosine distance).
Negative: If pgvector extension is missing/unavailable, semantic retrieval is disabled and the system degrades to lexical-only (explicitly observable in logs/debug endpoint).

stories.title: hybridSearch() returns ranked chunk hits and a debug endpoint makes tuning visible
stories.description: As a feature builder (chat, quick start), I want a single hybridSearch() function that returns ranked chunk IDs so that downstream features can rely on one retrieval contract.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-007: hybridSearch({ folderId, indexVersion, queryText, opts }) returns chunk_id, document_id, page_start, page_end; merged ranking from lexical + semantic branches; optional per-branch scores (lex_score, sem_score) for debugging.
AC-008: Default tuning is explicit: kLex=20, kSem=20, kFinal=10; lexWeight=0.55, semWeight=0.45.
AC-009: Dev-only debug endpoint exists under /spikes/retrieval/* to call hybridSearch() and inspect results.
AC-010: Logs include {nVectors, lists, probes, kLex, kSem, kFinal, hitCountsLex, hitCountsSem}.
AC-011: Small golden-questions smoke fixture exists (3-10 queries) asserting an expected doc/page appears in top K for a seeded fixture folder.
Example: Merge scoring is deterministic (same DB state + same query yields same ordered hits).

Negative: When semantic retrieval is unavailable (pgvector missing/unavailable), hybridSearch still returns results using lexical-only and reports the semantic branch as disabled (no silent pretending).
